title: Flat-pack bookcase
summary: CNC plywood, tusk tenons, cut list
description: An open bookcase of 18 mm birch plywood, CNC-routed from one 2500 x 1250 mm sheet and put together without screws, glue or tools: shelves and back rails pass through the sides in tusk tenons locked by tapered wedges.
process: CNC routing of plywood sheet, hand assembly with wedged through tenons, oil finish

difficulty.rationale: 28 plate bodies from four hand-built paths with dogbones and T-bones, about 60 coupled formulas, conditional parts, checks across bodies (interference, clearance, cut list, nesting) and expert joinery; no freeform.

standards: EN 315 (plywood thickness tolerances: 17.1 to 18.7 mm for 18 mm sanded, after the Handbook of Finnish Plywood, Table 2-3)
Handbook of Finnish Plywood (2002), Tables 3-1 and 3-2 (density, bending modulus)
Sagulator (woodbin.com): book load and shelf-sag target, span/600
materials: Birch plywood, 18 mm nominal (17.6 mm measured), 13 plies, EN 314-2 class 3, S/BB, oiled

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Passed: the four parts' volumes equal this example's to the mm³, 20.18 kg, 200 reliefs, 18.0 mm mortises, wedges bearing as here, no overlaps, sag 1.164 mm against 1.191 mm; builds at 3 and 5 shelves and the sheet, cutter and width limits. Found that cut.export's row layout overflows the sheet at five shelves (F-162). About 411 steps.
